title: Unify CPU hotpath: lightweight scheduler, zero-copy request path, and KV prefetch to reduce serialization
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: production workloads hitting inference control-plane observed sustained CPU saturation in the request hotpath even when GPU utilization was moderate. Root causes traced to (1) cyclical memcpy/parse steps copying request buffers between IO thread, dispatcher, and worker threads; (2) a single global dispatch mutex that serialized fast-path requests during bursts; (3) synchronous KV cache lookups that blocked worker threads and caused head-of-line stalls; (4) thread pool oversubscription and excessive spinning for short critical sections. This PR implements a series of coordinated CPU-side optimizations aimed at reducing serialization and context-switching friction while preserving correctness and fallbacks.Key changes (single-line summary): unified per-core cooperative scheduler, zero-copy request header handoff, KV-cache prefetch + lock-free read-path, striped dispatch slots and seqlock fallback, adjusted default thread pool sizing and soft-yield policy.Implementation details: - Introduced a lightweight per-core work scheduler (runtime/scheduler.cc) that keeps a small fixed set of worker contexts pinned to a core group and uses a M:N cooperative yield policy for short tasks (<= 4ms). Heavy tasks are demoted to the existing worker pool. This reduces cross-core wakeups for common fast-path requests.- Reworked request handoff to use reference-counted buffer views instead of copying headers into an intermediate struct. New zero-copy types live in runtime/io/buffer_view.h and replace ~3 memcpy sites in the hotpath. The public surface retains the same request API; ownership rules are documented in comments and unit tests.- KV cache: added an optimistic lock-free fast-path using atomic version stamps and an immutable backing array for small entries (runtime/kv_cache_fastpath.cc). For misses, we continue with existing shard+mutex path and schedule a low-priority async fetch so worker threads aren't blocked.- Dispatch: replaced the single global dispatch mutex with striped dispatch slots keyed by request hash (8 stripes). Short critical sections use seqlock to provide lockless reads with a mutex fallback on detected races.- Threading: tuned the default worker pool down from NCPU*1.5 to NCPU+2 and added a soft-yield (sched_yield + short nanosleep) for brief spin-wait loops to avoid burning CPU during transient contention.- Added detailed documentation in docs/perf/cpu-hotpath.md describing tradeoffs and rollout plan.Benchmarks: - Synthetic qps test (100ms GPU latency emulation, 2k concurrent clients): 18% lower p95 latency on the hotpath and 24% reduction in CPU sys time. - Production-like trace replay (mixed short chat/long generation): sustained throughput increased 12% with 10-12% lower CPU utilization at 95th percentile request rate.Rollout plan and safety: - Feature gated behind a runtime flag (runtime.flags.use_unified_scheduler). Disabled by default on Dedicated nodes until we finish long-tail stability testing. - Added runtime telemetry hooks: per-stripe contended_count, zero_copy_fallbacks, kv_prefetch_misses.- Includes a canary + stage rollout script (deploy/canary_unified_scheduler.sh) that coordinates enabling the flag per-pool and collects perf counters for 48h before wider rollout.Testing and QA: - Unit tests covering buffer_view ownership rules and concurrent fast-path reads. - Integration tests that simulate KV miss fallback and verify no deadlocks. - Stress harness recorded in perf/bench/repro_unified_scheduler that reproduces an earlier incident (INC-1124) locally. - Load tests run on staging clusters for 72h.Observability and metrics added: runtime.dispatch.stripe_latency, runtime.scheduler.task_demotes, runtime.kv_fastpath.hits/misses, and a new trace span (scheduler.handoff).CI and infra: - New lint rule added to ensure buffer_view is not copied by value (static analyzer plugin). - Several existing flaky tests were stabilized by reducing shared global state and adding proper teardown.Notes on tradeoffs and limitations: - Zero-copy only applies to requests that fit header+small metadata into contiguous buffers; large attachment streaming still copies. - The cooperative scheduler is tuned for short CPU bursts; workloads dominated by long CPU preprocessing should still use the heavy worker pool. - There is a small additional memory overhead for the immutable KV backing arrays (~2% resident memory in our staging profiles).Checklist:
- [x] Benchmarks attached and reproducible
- [x] Feature-flagged and documented
- [x] Integration and unit tests added
- [x] Rollout script included
- [x] Observability addedCommits summary: - a1f3e2b: add unified per-core scheduler and task demotion APIs - b4d9c8e: introduce buffer_view zero-copy types and replace hotpath copies - c7a12f4: add kv cache optimistic fast-path and prefetcher - d0e3ff1: replace global dispatch mutex with striped slots + seqlock fallback - e21b7a9: thread pool sizing and soft-yield logic; tests and docs - f6c3b2a: add canary deployment script and telemetry hooks

review_comments: Diego: Great direction. Please add a defensive assert in buffer_view to prevent accidental deep copy semantics. Also can we expose per-stripe counters to the console?
Author (Asha): Added debug-only assert and exported counters to telemetry. See docs/perf/cpu-hotpath.md for how to wire into Console.
Marta: Observed a small regression in long-running generator benchmarks in earlier iteration; how are you ensuring the cooperative scheduler doesn't starve long tasks?
Author (Asha): Scheduler demotes tasks > 4ms to the heavy pool; added integration test and a metric (task_demotes) so we can alert if demotion rate grows unexpectedly.
Elliot: CI initially failed with a race in kv_cache_fastpath tests; root cause was a missed fence. Fixed by adding atomic_thread_fence(seq_cst) on publish path.
release_notes: Reduced CPU-side serialization for common request hotpath: ~18% p95 latency reduction and ~24% CPU sys reduction in synthetic tests. Feature gated; enable via runtime.flags.use_unified_scheduler.
